stories.text: As a compositor, I want all eight requested nodes available through the ordinary node catalog, so that I can build practical compositions without private workflows.
As a Nuke compositor, I want familiar node roles, controls, defaults, and interactions, so that my existing compositing knowledge transfers to Nemo.
As a compositor, I want existing projects and accepted effects to retain their results during the foundation change, so that adding capabilities does not unexpectedly change my work.

As a compositor, I want a node's output format, data bounds, channels, pixel aspect, and interpretation to be described accurately, so that downstream effects process the actual image rather than assumptions.
As a compositor, I want pixels outside the image format and negative data-bound coordinates to remain representable where supported, so that overscan is not silently lost.
As a compositor, I want viewport regions and preview resolution to remain separate from authored image format, so that zooming or choosing Half does not change my composition.
As a compositor, I want Read and subsequent effects to preserve named auxiliary channels, so that masks and other image layers survive until I explicitly replace or remove them.
As a compositor, I want alpha-only and non-RGB data images handled deliberately, so that mask and data workflows do not require invented RGB content.
As a compositor, I want color channels distinguished from uninterpreted data channels, so that color management does not corrupt masks or auxiliary data.
As a compositor, I want alpha association to remain coherent across effects, so that transparent edges do not acquire double multiplication or unintended color changes.
As a compositor, I want invalid parameters and unavailable capabilities to identify the offending node and relationship, so that I can correct the problem rather than receive substituted pixels.

As a compositor, I want new node settings to use existing animation and exposed-parameter workflows where applicable, so that their behavior remains consistent inside Composition Networks and network instances.
As a compositor, I want edits, grouped gestures, cancellation, undo, and redo to use the common command history, so that new tools behave like established tools.
As a compositor, I want save/reopen to preserve authored node settings and recoverable unavailable-node data, so that my projects remain durable across application versions.
As a contributor, I want to add an ordinary effect through one contribution contract, so that I do not modify unrelated dispatch, editing, or presentation code.
As a contributor, I want unchanged image properties inherited through shared defaults, so that simple effects do not repeat every image rule.
As a contributor, I want my effect to declare output changes and per-input requirements, so that the shared planner can make correct requests without recognizing my node by name.
As a contributor, I want CPU reference and native GPU processing to consume the same resolved authored state, so that parameter, time, and input interpretation do not diverge.
As a contributor, I want independent numerical references and a real contribution example, so that extending the catalog has a clear correctness standard.
As a maintainer, I want coherent implementation, schema, and shader versioning, so that changed behavior cannot reuse incompatible cached results.
As a compositor, I want Shuffle to remap named channels within an image, so that I can rearrange render passes and masks.
As a compositor, I want Shuffle to source mappings from either of its two images, so that I can combine channels without changing the underlying sources.
As a compositor, I want one input channel to feed multiple output channels, so that I can replicate a matte or data value.
As a compositor, I want black and white constants as mapping sources, so that I can author zero and one without an extra image generator.
As a compositor, I want Shuffle to create named output channels and layers, so that I can organize auxiliary results for downstream processing and delivery.
As a compositor, I want untouched, missing, and disconnected channel mappings to follow an explicit Nuke-referenced policy, so that channels are not silently discarded or filled unpredictably.
As a compositor, I want a Nuke-referenced mapping editor integrated into the existing inspector, so that channel wiring remains understandable without a separate panel system.
As a compositor, I want Copy to replace channels in B with selected channels from A, so that donor and destination roles match Nuke.
As a compositor, I want individual channel pairs and layer/channel-set copying, so that I can transfer either a matte or multiple render passes.
As a compositor, I want unselected destination channels and the documented missing-donor behavior preserved, so that copying one channel does not damage others.
As a compositor, I want Copy's mask, inversion, and mix to blend against the original B input, so that partial copying behaves predictably.

As a compositor, I want the documented mask-injection, fringe, and optional unpremultiply/process/premultiply behavior accounted for, so that the coverage contract does not silently omit less-common Nuke controls.
As a compositor, I want Copy's union, A-side, and B-side bounding-box choices, so that I can control retained image coverage.
As a compositor, I want Copy's metadata and frame-range source policies represented, so that downstream information follows the chosen inputs.
As a compositor, I want Premult to multiply selected stored channels by a selected channel, so that I can explicitly premultiply an image.
As a compositor, I want Premult's channel selection and inversion controls, so that I can use alpha or another channel deliberately.
As a compositor, I want Unpremult to divide selected stored channels by a selected channel, so that I can prepare premultiplied color for correction.
As a compositor, I want Unpremult's channel selection and inversion controls, so that its operation corresponds to my intended divisor.
As a compositor, I want unselected channels preserved by both nodes, so that alpha and auxiliary data change only when selected.
As a compositor, I want zero, near-zero, negative, and HDR cases verified against the chosen reference contract, so that edge behavior is not an undocumented epsilon or clamp.
As a compositor, I want the Unpremult → Grade → Premult workflow to retain its authored meaning, so that automatic conversions neither cancel my operations nor apply them twice.

As a compositor, I want existing Merge, Blur, Transform, source interpretation, and viewer behavior reconciled with explicit association changes, so that new nodes do not create inconsistent downstream processing.
As a compositor, I want an animatable crop box with Nuke-referenced coordinate and extent controls, so that I can define the area to retain precisely.
As a compositor, I want to edit the crop box through native viewer handles, so that I can position it visually.
As a compositor, I want Crop to change data bounds without necessarily changing format, so that I can remove unwanted image coverage while retaining the canvas.
As a compositor, I want Crop's reformat option to make the output format match the cropped image, so that downstream nodes see the intended dimensions and coordinates.
As a compositor, I want intersection and non-intersection bounding-box modes, so that the crop can either respect or extend incoming coverage.
As a compositor, I want softness and black-outside/edge-extension behavior to match the reference, so that cropped edges behave correctly when composited.

As a compositor, I want offset boxes, empty resulting data bounds, odd dimensions, and absent-alpha cases handled explicitly, so that cropping never produces mislabeled rasters or invalid memory access.
As a compositor, I want Reformat's to-format, to-box, and scale modes, so that I can author delivery and working image sizes.
As a compositor, I want reusable named formats and a persistent composition-format fallback, so that generators and Reformat resolve dimensions without relying on the selected viewer or source.
As a compositor, I want pixel aspect and aspect-preserving resize modes, so that anamorphic and square-pixel images retain the intended shape.
As a compositor, I want width, height, fit, fill, none, and distort behavior accounted for, so that the chosen sizing policy matches Nuke.
As a compositor, I want centering, alignment, flip, flop, and turn behavior defined, so that format conversion positions the image predictably.
As a compositor, I want filter selection, clamp, black-outside, and bounding-box preservation matched to the declared reference, so that resampling quality and overscan remain under my control.
As a compositor, I want precise rounding and coordinate behavior at odd sizes and fractional scales, so that CPU, GPU, full-frame, and regional results agree within the declared tolerance.
As a compositor, I want chains with differently sized inputs and multiple format changes to evaluate correctly, so that a Composition Network is not restricted to one global canvas.
As a compositor, I want a Roto node that creates vector mattes with a background or as a generator, so that I can isolate image areas without external mask files.
As a compositor, I want Bézier and B-spline shapes, including the reference's basic shape tools, so that I can choose the appropriate contour representation.
As a compositor, I want to add, remove, select, move, smooth, and cusp points and edit tangents or tension, so that I can refine shapes with familiar interactions.
As a compositor, I want per-point feather and the documented feather controls, so that matte edges can vary along a contour.
As a compositor, I want stable shape identities and a shape/group hierarchy with visibility, locking, inversion, and ordering, so that complex mattes remain editable.
As a compositor, I want shape/group transforms and defined blending behavior, so that multiple shapes combine predictably.
As a compositor, I want shape geometry and relevant properties to animate with explicit key and interpolation behavior, so that a matte can follow movement over time.
As a compositor, I want shape lifetime ranges and activation behavior, so that elements can contribute only where intended.

As a compositor, I want output channels, replacement, premultiplication, input masking, and clipping policies accounted for, so that Roto integrates with the same channel and bounds model as other nodes.
As a compositor, I want input-connected and generator format resolution to follow the reference, so that the same node behaves predictably with or without a background.
As a compositor, I want the reference's shape/global motion-blur modes, shutter controls, and sampling behavior represented, so that moving shapes produce intentional temporal coverage.
As a compositor, I want shape editing, including interrupted gestures, to use the existing undo/redo and persistence workflow, so that edits cannot leave a second hidden state behind.

As a compositor, I want Roto handles and hit testing to remain correct under viewer zoom, pan, pixel aspect, preview scale, and upstream format changes, so that displayed handles coincide with rendered contours.
As a compositor, I want dense animated shape sets to remain responsive during evaluation, so that rendering does not block authoring.

As a compositor, I want Write nodes to branch from any compatible point and remain distinct from formal Output and display-only Viewer roles, so that delivery does not redefine the Composition Network's result.
As a compositor, I want ordinary evaluation through a Write node to remain side-effect-free, so that playback and inspection never create or overwrite files.
As a compositor, I want to explicitly submit one or more Write jobs with chosen frame ranges, so that rendering happens only on request.
As a compositor, I want file patterns and output frame-number mapping, so that image-sequence names match the intended delivery range.
As a compositor, I want selectable channels, supported output formats, precision, compression, and metadata settings, so that delivered files preserve the required information.
As a compositor, I want EXR delivery to preserve selected named channels, pixel aspect, and supported display/data windows, so that multilayer and overscan workflows round-trip.
As a compositor, I want output color conversion, Raw/Data handling, and alpha treatment to use project color policy, so that a deliverable is not accidentally a baked viewer preview.
As a compositor, I want quality and resolution stated on the job, so that preview or proxy data cannot silently satisfy a full-quality delivery.
As a compositor, I want output collisions, directory creation, and overwrite policy resolved before destructive writing, so that existing files are not silently replaced.
As a compositor, I want progress, cancellation, and file-specific errors, so that I know what completed and what remains unfinished.
As a compositor, I want failed or cancelled output to be distinguishable from a successfully completed frame or movie, so that partial files cannot masquerade as valid delivery.
As a compositor, I want an accepted job to retain a stable Document snapshot and settings, so that later edits do not silently alter frames midway through the job.
As a compositor, I want delivery work to share bounded scheduling and resource accounting without blocking interaction, so that I can continue editing while it runs.
As an automation author, I want the UI and CLI to submit and inspect the same delivery jobs, so that scripted rendering has the same semantics as manual rendering.
As a compositor, I want document undo to remain distinct from external file effects, so that undo never claims to reverse an export that already occurred.
As a compositor, I want regional requests to render the same result as the corresponding region of a full-frame evaluation, so that zooming cannot change edge or channel behavior.
As a compositor, I want unaffected branches and compatible covered regions to remain reusable, so that unrelated edits and small pans do not discard valid work.
As a compositor, I want changes to format, bounds, channels, alpha/color interpretation, or implementation identity to prevent incompatible reuse, so that cached images never have the wrong meaning.
As a compositor, I want cancelled or superseded work excluded from current publication while its GPU resources remain alive until completion, so that responsiveness does not introduce corruption.

As a compositor, I want intermediate, scratch, retained, and delivery resources admitted against byte budgets, so that larger formats and additional channels do not turn a small entry count into uncontrolled memory pressure.
As a compositor, I want eligible cached resources evicted before an avoidable allocation failure, so that valid work can continue within configured budgets.
As a compositor, I want an explicit limitation when the active working set cannot fit, so that the engine does not silently reduce channels, quality, or precision.
As a maintainer, I want native effects to remain device-resident and batch compatible work without per-node host waits, so that adding effects does not introduce serial readback bottlenecks.
As a maintainer, I want visible latency, cold/warm behavior, transfers, and memory measured on declared workloads, so that optimization decisions reflect real costs rather than shader-only timing.
As a contributor, I want a genuinely new capability implemented in its owning module and reused by later effects, so that future coverage expands without parallel frameworks or node-name exceptions.
